text:
Raj: Heads-up — Prospect (GlacierTech) wants a Private/VPC POC next week. Requirements: SAML SSO that never leaves their private network, prefer dual-stack v4/v6 for app traffic, and a short non-technical justification comparing PrivateLink vs Peering for their security reviewers. Can NetOps + Sec advise?

Leah: Quick summary for reviewers: PrivateLink = endpoint-level isolation + simpler firewall allowlist and no cross-account routing. VPC Peering = lower connector fees and simpler L3 routing but exposes broader network reachability and requires careful route table scoping. If "no internet transit" for SAML is strict, Private deployment or a hybrid approach is safer.

Mike: IPv6 detail: our hosted PrivateLink connector currently speaks IPv4 only. We support IPv6-to-IPv4 via a customer-side NAT64/NAT64+DNS64 setup. Native v6 data plane is not GA. If GlacierTech needs native IPv6 for inference traffic, that's a blocker for PrivateLink hosted at GA. Control-plane (SAML) can be proxied over IPv4 PrivateLink.

Sam: Security POV: if SAML assertions must not exit the customer VPC, they either need: 1) private deployment (control plane inside their network) OR 2) a small SAML proxy/bridge inside their VPC that forwards assertions to our control plane over PrivateLink. Mark requirement as HIGH risk for hosted control-plane. Also call out TLS inspection — if they perform TLS MITM, they'll need to whitelist our endpoints or accept our certs.

Raj: They also asked about pricing — any extra recurring fees for PrivateLink connector?

Leah: Yes: hosted PrivateLink has a monthly connector surcharge + per-GB egress charge. Private deployment is a separate licensing model (platform + support). I'll follow up with the exact pricing line after the sync.

Mike: Draft minimal firewall allowlist for their NetOps team (example CIDRs are placeholders):
```
# Outbound from customer app/subnets to Redwood endpoints
TCP 443 -> 34.210.128.0/22   # control-plane callbacks / auth
TCP 443 -> 52.204.16.0/22    # model-serving endpoints (hosted)
# Optional: ICMP echo to 34.210.128.0/22 for health checks
# If static egress required: allow TCP 443 from our EIP pool (we will share exact IPs)
```

Sam: Note: If perimeter performs SNI-based TLS inspection, they must either allow SNI passthrough for our hostnames or install our CA cert for that inspection device; otherwise SAML postbacks may fail. Also list acceptable cipher suites and minimum TLS 1.2.

Raj: GlacierTech insists on v6 for client-facing app traffic but control-plane SAML can be private-only. Can we deliver a step plan for the POC?

Mike: POC preflight checklist to hand them: 1) Provide a VPC (/20 recommended) or designate existing VPC + spare private subnets. 2) Reserve two private subnets for connector components (no public IPs). 3) Pre-authorize outbound HTTPS to our control-plane CIDRs (we'll provide exact ranges). 4) If they want v6 app traffic: deploy NAT64/DNS64 or use an IPv6-to-IPv4 translation gateway for connector subnets. 5) If SAML must stay private: deploy tiny SAML bridge in their VPC that proxies to control-plane over PrivateLink. 6) Optional: request static egress IPs if their IdP or callback ACLs need them — we'll provide EIP list.

Leah: I'll draft the one-page justification memo (PrivateLink vs Peering) for their security team: focus on attack surface, routing scope, and management overhead.

Sam: I'll prepare redlined answers to their security questionnaire and mark the SAML-private constraint as a gating item for hosted control-plane. Also include guidance on logging/audit exports and KMS expectations.

Raj: Can we meet today at 3:30pm PT to finalize the checklist and the firewall snippet before I send it to the customer?

Leah: 3:30 works. @Mike @Sam?

Mike: Yes — I'll bring the exact connector CIDRs and sample route table changes.

Sam: In. I'll bring the questionnaire and the list of acceptable crypto profiles.

security-bot: GlacierTech checked the box "no shared IPs". PrivateLink provides per-endpoint isolation but not necessarily dedicated physical hosts. If they require dedicated hardware/host tenancy, open an Ops ticket for dedicated-hosting options. :lock:

Raj: Perfect. I'll schedule and send a concise POC pre-provision checklist to GlacierTech after the call. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
